context.requirement_text: Settle OQ-6 -- Lua 5.3 integer/float marshalling across VariableMerge and JSONB variable storage (blocks LUA-11 / REQ-159 / REQ-160). Design-only requirement; no lib/letflow/engine/ change.

task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md against REQ-150's acceptance criteria, re-running at least one empirical claim rather than trusting the doc's prose.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md exists with a numbered normative section stating one rule per direction (Lua to Elixir, Elixir to Lua) that REQ-159 and REQ-160 can cite by section number

the artefact quotes real runs showing what an Elixir integer, an Elixir float, a Lua integer, and a Lua float each become on crossing the boundary in the adopted runtime -- observed, not inferred from the Lua 5.3 manual
the artefact states explicitly what happens to a float with no fractional part (e.g. 2.0) after a Jason.encode!/Jason.decode! round trip, with the real output quoted
the artefact states the behaviour for an integer outside IEEE-754 exact range and for a JSON null, each with a defined outcome rather than 'undefined'
the artefact names the exact module and function that will own the conversion
the artefact states that WASM-12's parity requirement (REQ-171, REQ-172) binds the WASM half to this same rule, citing decision 0014's OQ-6
no file under lib/letflow/engine/ is modified by this requirement, confirmed by `git diff --stat` scoped to its commits

result.summary: Verified lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md against all 7 acceptance criteria plus the general design-gate checks (no TBD/deferral language, fully specified signatures with error shape stated, cross-module dependencies listed, no implementation code present). AC1: SS2.1 (Lua->Elixir) and SS2.2 (Elixir->Lua) are the two numbered per-direction normative rules, explicitly citable as 'REQ-150 SS2.n', with SS2.6 as a consolidated summary table. AC2-AC7 all backed by quoted real runs in SS1 (SS1.1 Lua literal->Elixir, SS1.2 Elixir->Lua via Lua.set!/3, SS1.3/1.5 Jason whole-number-float round trip, SS1.6 2^53+1 exact round trip, SS1.7 real disposable-Postgres jsonb column round trip, SS1.8 JSON null<->nil<->Lua nil, SS4 WASM-12/decision-0014-OQ-6 binding statement, SS6 git diff --stat scoped to lib/letflow/engine/). Independently re-ran (not merely re-read) four of the doc's empirical claims via `MIX_ENV=test mix run --no-start` against this checkout's real tv-labs/lua 1.0.2 dep and real Jason: (1) Jason.encode!(3)=='3', Jason.encode!(3.0)=='3.0', decode('3')->3 (integer,not float), decode('3.0')->3.0 (float,not integer) -- exact match to doc SS1.3/SS1.5, confirming the whole-number-float-does-not-collapse claim myself rather than trusting the doc's prose; (2) 2^53+1 (9007199254740993) round-tripped through Jason.encode!/decode! byte-exact, is_integer true -- matches SS1.6; (3) Lua.set!/3 with Elixir 42 and 42.0 followed by `return math.type(...)` inside the real VM returned 'integer' and 'float' respectively -- matches SS1.2's core claim exactly; (4) Elixir nil set into Lua state and compared with `== nil` inside a script returned the 'lua_nil' sentinel string proving Lua-side nil identity -- matches SS1.8. Also independently checked citations: postgrex/lib/postgrex/extensions/jsonb.ex line 8 in this checkout's deps/ is exactly `Application.get_env(:postgrex, :json_library, Jason)` as quoted, and `grep -rn json_library config/` confirms no override, so the doc's 'this app configures no override' claim holds. `git diff --stat main...HEAD` confirms only the design .md and handoff .json changed -- zero lib/letflow/engine/ touches, satisfying AC7. Owning module SS3 names Letflow.Engine.LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1 and .from_lua/1 with full term()->term() signatures, explicit identity-function behaviour for the in-scope numeric/nil cases, an explicit 'both functions are total (no error return)' error-shape statement, and an explicit scope boundary excluding non-numeric types -- no ambiguity left for REQ-159/REQ-160 to guess at. Cross-module dependents (VariableMerge.merge/3, Ecto :map field, Jason, Postgrex jsonb extension) are named with file:line pointers. No TBD/deferral language anywhere in the document; SS5 explicitly states 'None' open questions and scopes the one deferred item (non-numeric marshalling) rather than silently omitting it. No .ex implementation file exists or was created -- SS3 states this explicitly and it is confirmed by directory listing. One trivial nit found, not a gate failure: SS1.7's line citation for the variables field ('instance_projections.variables ... instance_projection.ex:133') is off by two lines in this checkout (actual field is at line 135); the content of the citation (a plain Ecto :map field) is correct, only the line number has drifted, most likely from an intervening unrelated edit to that file -- does not affect any acceptance criterion or the design's correctness, flagged for CODE-DESIGNER/DOC-UPDATER awareness only, not a rework trigger.
issues: Minor (non-blocking): SS1.7 cites lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex:133 for the `variables` field; in this checkout it is actually at line 135. Content of the citation is correct (plain Ecto :map field); only the line number has drifted.
